name: param-uq-00-screen
title: Parameter screen — which config-reachable knobs actually drive the observables?
claim:
Of the top-level process-config knobs reachable via `baseline()` config_overrides,
only 3 produce a real change in growth rate; the rest are inert.
question:
Among the top-level `ecoli-*` process-config scalars, which actually change the
growth observables when perturbed (so they're worth including in the UQ)?

report.title: param-uq-00-screen — parameter screen for UQ-eligible config knobs
report.evidence_quality: low/high sweep per knob, 120-step window, 7 candidates screened
report.objective:
Before investing in a full PCE-based UQ (param-uq-01), identify which
top-level `ecoli-*` process-config scalars actually change the simulation's
growth observables. This avoids wasting surrogate budget on inert parameters
and ensures the effective parameter surface is well-defined.
report.setup:
Method: vary each candidate knob between a "low" and "high" bound (physically
meaningful range) with a FRESH initial_state (v2ecoli PR #197) to prevent
state-carryover. Run a 120-step window and measure % change in
`instantaneous_growth_rate` (low → high swing).

Candidate knobs screened (7 total from ecoli-polypeptide-elongation and
ecoli-chromosome-replication process configs).
report.result:
Screen %-response (instantaneous_growth_rate, low→high swing):

| Knob | Path | % response | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| basal_elongation_rate | ecoli-polypeptide-elongation.basal_elongation_rate | 13.8% | EFFECTIVE |
| kS | ecoli-polypeptide-elongation.kS | 5.5% | EFFECTIVE |
| chrom basal_elongation_rate | ecoli-chromosome-replication.basal_elongation_rate | 2.8% | EFFECTIVE |
| k_RelA | ecoli-polypeptide-elongation.k_RelA | 1.4% | inert |
| gtpPerElongation | ecoli-polypeptide-elongation.gtpPerElongation | 0.0% | inert |
| import_threshold | ecoli-polypeptide-elongation.import_threshold | 0.0% | inert |
| D_period | ecoli-chromosome-replication.D_period | 0.0% | inert |

Note: ribosomeElongationRate is inert because it is overwritten at runtime each
step (the config value is ignored). gtpPerElongation only affects energy
accounting and does not move the growth-rate observable. The 3 effective knobs
feed param-uq-01.
report.interpretation:
config_overrides reach only top-level process knobs; most physiological params
live deeper in sim_data and are not reachable by this path (see param-uq-04).
This screen defines the effective UQ surface for the config_overrides path.
The 3 EFFECTIVE knobs (basal_elongation_rate, kS, chrom.basal_elongation_rate)
form the parameter set for param-uq-01-elongation.
report.decision:
PASS — screen complete. 3 of 7 screened knobs show >2% growth-rate response
and are included in the UQ. The inert knobs are excluded from the UQ budget.
See param-uq-04-deep-params for the path to deeper sim_data parameters.

model_settings.detail: Each low/high perturbation uses a fresh initial_state (v2ecoli PR #197) to prevent state carryover across samples.

model_settings.name: growth-rate-observable
model_settings.detail: Observable = instantaneous_growth_rate; chosen because mass observables do not respond over a 120-step window.

model_settings.name: threshold-2pct
model_settings.detail: Knobs with >2% response are classified EFFECTIVE; ≤1.4% classified inert.

assumptions.text:
config_overrides at the `baseline()` call reach only top-level process-config
scalars. Deep sim_data physiological parameters (kinetic rates, mass fractions)
are not reachable by this path and were not screened here.

A 120-step window (fresh initial_state, ~4% of one generation) is sufficient to
reveal whether a knob has a real effect on instantaneous_growth_rate. Knobs
that modulate slower timescale processes may appear inert at this window.

tests.name: screen-identifies-effective-knobs
tests.question:
Do at least 1 of the 7 screened config-reachable knobs show a >2% response
in instantaneous_growth_rate (i.e., is the UQ parameter surface non-trivial)?

measure.detail:
3 of 7 screened knobs show >2% growth-rate response (basal_elongation_rate
13.8%, kS 5.5%, chrom.basal_elongation_rate 2.8%). Measured value = 3
effective knobs identified.

tests.cites_note: Methodological screening threshold (>2% growth-rate response); not literature-derived.

if_primary_tests_pass.interpretation:
At least one config-reachable knob moves instantaneous_growth_rate >2%, so the
config_overrides path exposes a non-trivial UQ surface. The 3 EFFECTIVE knobs
(basal_elongation_rate 13.8%, kS 5.5%, chrom.basal_elongation_rate 2.8%) become
the parameter set for param-uq-01; the 4 inert knobs are excluded from the
surrogate budget.
pipeline_unblocks: param-uq-01-elongation runs forward UQ on exactly these 3 effective knobs.

diagnose: If 0 of 7 knobs cleared >2%, either the 120-step window is too short to expose elongation effects, or config_overrides are not reaching the process configs (re-test against a known-responsive knob before widening the candidate list).
if_primary_tests_fail.block_downstream: param-uq-01-elongation would have no effective surface to sample and should not start.

conclusion_verdicts.claim: Only a minority of config-reachable knobs drive the growth observable.
conclusion_verdicts.basis: 3 of 7 screened knobs cleared >2% (basal 13.8%, kS 5.5%, chrom 2.8%); 4 inert.

conclusion_verdicts.claim: ribosomeElongationRate and gtpPerElongation are inert for growth rate.

study_card.goal:
Screen the 7 top-level ecoli-* process-config scalars reachable via baseline()
config_overrides to find which actually move the growth observable, defining the
effective parameter surface before investing surrogate budget (param-uq-01).
study_card.why_before_next:
A forward-UQ surrogate spends its sample budget per parameter; screening out the
inert knobs (4 of 7 here) keeps param-uq-01's PCE focused on the 3 knobs that
carry real growth-rate signal.

biological_summary:
Three elongation-related rates move instantaneous growth rate: ribosome translation
speed (basal_elongation_rate, default 22 aa/s), the ppGpp/charging saturation
constant kS, and the DNA-polymerase elongation rate. The other candidates are inert
for growth rate — ribosomeElongationRate is overwritten at runtime each step, and
gtpPerElongation only enters GTP/energy accounting — so they carry no growth signal
at a 120-step window.

literature_anchors.expectation:
The baseline knob values (ribosome basal_elongation_rate ~22 aa/s, DNA-pol
elongation ~967 nt/s) come from the wcEcoli/v2ecoli mechanistic parameterization.
literature_anchors.status_in_workspace: Verified — the screen perturbs around these documented defaults.

model_change.notes:
No model change — this is a pure sensitivity screen of existing config knobs via
baseline() config_overrides. The only methodological requirement is a fresh
initial_state per perturbation (v2ecoli PR #197) to keep samples independent.

implementation_requirements.title: Fresh initial_state per perturbation
implementation_requirements.description:
Each low/high run deep-copies the baseline initial_state (v2ecoli PR #197) so
samples are independent; without it dry_mass climbs by sample index (the
state-carryover artifact that produced the original spurious dominance reading).

design_pivot_required.question: Is the config_overrides path sufficient to screen the full physiological parameter space?
design_pivot_required.decision:
NO. config_overrides reach only top-level process-config scalars; most physiological
parameters live deeper in sim_data and are unreachable by this path. Deep params are
deferred to param-uq-04-deep-params (sim_data-level injection + ParCa rebuild).
alternatives: Treat config-reachable knobs as the full surface (rejected — misses sim_data params).
Add sim_data-level injection now (deferred to param-uq-04 as a separate infra task).

falsifiability:
The screen's classification fails if a knob it flags EFFECTIVE
(basal_elongation_rate) does not move instantaneous_growth_rate on a fresh
initial_state, or if a knob it flags inert (D_period and the other ~0%-effect
knobs) does move it. A reordering of the per-knob effect column would refute
the "which knobs actually drive the observable" conclusion.
